sources.summary: HostDime Colombia's own post (author Organization 'HostDime Colombia', signed 'Equipo HostDime Colombia') reports that on 28 August 2026 the Uptime Institute issued the Tier IV Facility certification for Data Center Nebula, the certification granted on the built installation in operation ('sobre la instalación construida y en operación'), after field tests of generators, fuel systems, UPS, switchgear and cooling carried out with the operation running, which demonstrated the fault tolerance of Nebula's 2N configuration. Slide 30 reports Q3 2026 cabinets billed and recurring revenues for the 193 stabilized, 52 expansion and 12 new IBX data centers (257 in all). sources.title: Iron Mountain Q3 2026 Supplemental Financial Information (Data Center Operating Portfolio and Expansion and Development Activity)
sources.summary: Iron Mountain's 29-page supplemental for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, released with its 5 November 2026 results ('All figures for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 unless noted'). Page 22, 'Data Center Operating Portfolio', has an India row 'MUM-1/2 and Other' with 11.8 stabilized leaseable MW (73.9% leased by MW), 1.5 pre-stabilized MW and 13.3 MW in all (65.5% leased); the same page lists the operating portfolio as 544.6 MW against 317.1 MW under construction and 511.9 MW held for development. In the second-quarter supplemental the India row was labelled 'Web Werks'. Page 23, 'Data Center Expansion and Development Activity', lists under India New Development 'MUM-3' (51.5 MW under construction, 100% pre-leased, Q3 investment $3.7M, cumulative $35.6M, expected completion Q3 2028) and 'CHN-1' (23.2 MW under construction, 100% pre-leased, Q3 investment $13.1M, cumulative $77.0M, expected completion Q4 2027), plus 72.8 MW of India future phases held for development and 3.8 MW of India expansion under construction ('Other'). The definitions page defines Pre-Stabilized as 'A building recently placed in service which has not yet reached 85% leased or 24 months in service'. The supplemental thus states that MUM-1 and MUM-2 are in Iron Mountain's operating data-centre portfolio at 30 September 2026. It gives no address, and MW figures are leaseable capacity, not measured load.
